rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Easy reckoning is mere presentation of the record; whoever is closely questioned in the account perishes.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ يُحَاسَبُ إِلاَّ هَلَكَ

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha asks how easy reckoning fits the verse; the Prophet says presentation is not scrutiny, which destroys the one questioned.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den rivayet etmişlerdir: “Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet prayed for easy reckoning and explained it as looking at the record and overlooking sins; the cited report is graded sound.
rows.anchor: sahih diye yine Hazret-i Âişe’den rivayet etmişlerdir ki: “Resûlullah’ı dinledim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The happy believer returns to his people and invites them to read his book; these people include believing companions and family, and the heavenly companions prepared for him.
rows.anchor: Ehli, mü’minlerden olan yârânı ve müte‘allikātı ve Allah teâlâ’nın cennette

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the book behind one’s back corresponds to receiving it in the left hand elsewhere; both signal reversal, ill fortune, hardship, humiliation, and danger.
rows.anchor: İkisinde de terslik, şeâmet, zorluk, hakāret ve tehlike mânası vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain that the right hand is tied to the neck and the left behind the back, so the book is handed from behind.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da “sağ eli boynuna, sol eli arkasına bağlanıp kitabı arkasının gerisinden verilir” demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left hand signifies ill fortune and reversed deeds, while the book behind the back signifies the weight of punishment carried on the back.
rows.anchor: Soldan verilmesi şeâmet ve ma‘kûsiyetine, arkasından verilmesi de وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book behind the back may also recall those who cast God’s Book behind them, or the unexpected adverse announcement made without regard for them.
rows.anchor: فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ [Âl-i İmrân 3/187] medlûlünce dünyada Kitabullâh’ı arkalarına atıp zıddına gittikleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sübūr means destruction: the condemned cries for destruction to come and rescue him from distress, then enters the blazing Fire.
rows.anchor: “Sübûr” helâk demektir. Yani “vâ sübûrâ: ey helâk! Nerdesin gel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His worldly happiness among family and people meant comfort and pleasure; he ignored the afterlife, suffering people, and worldly change.
rows.anchor: Dünyada, evinde, ailesi, kavmi içinde ferahlı, refahlı[^24], keyfi yerinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He assumed he would never return or undergo reversal, that his joy would not become grief, and that he would neither die nor face punishment or accountability.
rows.anchor: asla dönmeyecek, inkılâb görmeyecek sürûru kedere çevrilmeyecek, ölmeyecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawr is a return from completion to diminution and loss, like decline after increase, corruption after righteousness, or regression after progress.
rows.anchor: “Havr” bir kemâlden sonra noksan ve zevâle rücû‘ve inkılâbdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic supplication seeks refuge from decline after increase, illustrating hawr as reversal from improvement to loss.
rows.anchor: bir hadîs-i şerîfte نـَعُوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الْحَوْرِ بـَعْدَ الْكَوْرِ “kevrden sonra havrden Allah’a sığınırız”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrary to his assumption, the person will undergo reversal and return to God through death and resurrection, as the preceding verse says.
rows.anchor: Burada إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ buyurulduğu üzere mevt ve ba‘s ile Allah’a rücû‘dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees and watches all his deeds, so He will bring him back, reckon with him, and requite him.
rows.anchor: Bütün yaptıklarını görüp gözetip duruyor. Binâen‘aleyh onu kaçırmaz, behemehâl çevirecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening particle draws the conclusion and affirmation from the preceding exposition.
rows.anchor: فاء Geçen beyânât üzerine neticeyi tefrî‘ve takrirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shafaq is the red glow on the horizon after sunset; its root connotes delicacy, as do compassion and fearful concern.
rows.anchor: “Şefak” akşam güneş battıktan sonra ufukta görünen kırmızılığın ismidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, legal usage, and astronomy, shafaq is the post-sunset red opposite dawn and marks Maghrib; Turkish use for dawn is colloquial.
rows.anchor: Arapça’da ve ıstılâh-ı şer‘de ve hey’etçiler ıstılâhında “şafak”, fecre mukabil olarak gurubdan sonraki kırmızılıktır

rows.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa identifies shafaq as the whiteness that follows the red glow; Abu Hurayra and Umar b. Abd al-Aziz are also reported to hold this view, and Abu Hanifa’s later return to the majority view is transmitted.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe Hazretleri kırmızılıktan sonraki beyazlık olduğuna kāil olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath evokes the changing scenes of the world, with each day turning toward evening, first the red twilight and then night and what it gathers.
rows.anchor: burada murad dünyâ hayat ile mesrur olanlara karşı her gün[^30] bir akşama müncer olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasq means to gather, collect, accumulate, or load; the night’s gathering is what it collects, while ittiṣāq denotes orderly arrangement.
rows.anchor: “Vesak” zamm ve cem‘, yani derleyip toplamak, biriktirip yüklenmek mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths culminate in the moon at full, when it has gathered into a regular whole; these changing heavenly states illustrate people’s passage through successive states toward their Lord.
rows.anchor: Kamer’e yani derlenip toplanarak muntazam bedr olduğu zaman Ay’a kasem edilip de buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabaq has a broad range: something matching another, a cover, pair, vessel, layer or rank, state, generation or era, twenty years, spinal bones, a mountain, or the earth.
rows.anchor: bir şeyin kapağına veya örtüsüne ve bir çiftin teki gibi mutâbık ve uygununa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broadest interpretation is that people pass from one state matching another into successive states; some restrict this to severe hardship, which the author finds unsupported.
rows.anchor: Burada en ziyade “yekdiğerine mutâbık hâlden hâle geçeceksiniz” diye tefsir edilmiştir ki en şümullü mânası budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the phrase as movement from one layer, generation, or century to another, or as changes every twenty years.
rows.anchor: Bazıları karndan karna, asırdan asra demişler, bazıları da yirmi seneden yirmi seneye tehavvülâta işaret

rows.speaker: Mekhul
rows.claim: Mekhul says that every twenty years people find themselves in a condition they had not previously experienced.
rows.anchor: Mekhul demiştir ki: “Her yirmi senede evvel bulunmadığınız bir hâlde bulunursunuz.”

rows.speaker: İbn Münzir ve İbn Ebî Hâtim
rows.claim: Their report says that every twenty years people bring about an affair they had not previously encountered.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir’in ve İbn Ebî Hâtim’in rivayetinde de her yirmi senede evvel üzerinde bulunmadığınız bir emr ihdas edersiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the transition as one human community after another; Abbas’s poem depicts a new, superior generation appearing as one world passes.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Abbas b. Abdülmuttalib medhederken şöyle demişti: وَأَنْتَ لَمَّا وُلِدْتَ أَ شْرَقَتِ الْ أَرْضُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These views all express that individuals and societies never remain fixed but keep changing until they return to God and are judged.
rows.anchor: insanların gerek ferd ve gerek cemiyet itibariyle hayatta bir kararı olmayıp ölüm ve âhirete doğru Allah’a rücû‘edinceye kadar tehavvülden tehavvüle geçmeye mahkum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukūb can be literal or metaphorical for transition and encounter: one state meets or overtakes another without becoming identical in essence, whether the states differ or share a kind.
rows.anchor: Hâlin hâle mutabakatı ikinci hâlin evvelkine bir hadde telâkīsi veya galebesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of riding from layer to layer pictures a journey of change that may ascend or descend; worldly life is a passage, and the afterlife is permanence in joy or Hell.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle rukûb ve tabakta bir yolculuk, ya yukarı veya aşağı giden bir inkılâb tasvir ve tehyîci vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing everyone makes this change both promise and warning; addressing the Prophet and believers promises a sure return and calls them to keep rising toward God.
rows.anchor: bu ihbarda inkılâbın terakki veya tedennî olabilmesi itibariyle bir cihetten vaad, bir cihetten va‘îd vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religious spirit is ordered, stepwise progress toward meeting God, neither inert attachment to custom nor purposeless novelty; equal days mean loss.
rows.anchor: bir hadîs-i şerifte مَنِ اسْتـَوَى يـَوْمَاهُ فـَهُوَ مَغْبُونٌ “iki günü müsâvî olan aldanmıştır”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the full moon signals the promised uplift beyond worldly transitions.
rows.anchor: Bunda insanı bütün inkılâbâtın fevkine çıkaracak bir terakki düstûru

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the singular reading with fatḥa, the address can be to Muhammad alone and promise his ascent through heavens, ranks, and closeness to God on the Night Journey; this is reported from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: با’nın fethiyle müfred olarak لَتَرْكَبُنَّ kıraatine göre hitab evvelemirde Peygamber’e ait

rows.speaker: إبن عباس و إبن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud transmit the interpretation that the singular address promises the Prophet ascent from heaven to heaven during the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas ve İbn Mes‘ûd’dan rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: مُجَاهِد
rows.claim: Mujahid’s interpretation from Ibn Abbas says the phrase means state after state and refers to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de Mücâhid’den İbn Abbas, لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍۢ “hâlen ba‘de hâlin” dedi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the plural reading with ḍamma, the address includes Muslims following the Prophet, who rise toward God as they follow him; those who oppose this path are overcome.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde با’nın zammıyla cemi‘olarak لَتَرْكَبُنَّ kıraati de Peygamber’le beraber ona ittibâ‘eden müslimîne hitab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states a general law of life’s ascent or decline through successive states and generations; the highest life corresponds to the highest environment, God.
rows.anchor: en yüksek hayat, en yüksek muhîte mutabakat demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is the fullest life; reaching it requires continuing toward God without stopping at lesser aims and obeying His command at each turn.
rows.anchor: O’na yükselmek için de O’ndan beride hiçbir gaye ve maksadda durup kalmamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in the changing world endures; those who refuse to go willingly will be forced to God in the terror of resurrection, deprived of honor and subject to His majesty.
rows.anchor: Allah’a tav‘an gitmek istemeyen nasıl olsa kerhen gidecek ve o kıyametin şiddet ve hevli içinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since worldly change and return to God are unavoidable, the deniers have no reason to reject belief or neglect good works; they cannot remain in their present state.
rows.anchor: Hakikat böyle iken, yani beyan olunduğu üzere bu dünyada inkılâb muhakkak, tabaktan tabaka tehavvülât ile âhirete gitmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Quran is recited, they neither prostrate nor submit to its truth and commands.
rows.anchor: secde etmezler boyun eğmezler, hakikati [5684] teslim etmezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited 96:19 and prostrated, the believers followed, and Quraysh clapped and whistled; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselam bir gün وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب [el-Alâk 96/19] okumuş da secde etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa infers that prostration at this recitation is obligatory, while Shafii calls it Sunnah; Ibn Abbas is reported to deny prostrations in the Mufassal surahs.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe Hazretleri bununla burada secde-i tilâvetin vücûbuna istidlâl eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra swore that he prostrated after seeing the Prophet do so here; Anas says Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali also prostrated in prayer.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre radıyallahu anh burada secde etmiş ve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the surah is recited through its end before bowing, the prayer’s bowing and prostration suffice for the recitation prostration; Hasan’s report that it is not obligatory is understood this way.
rows.anchor: sûrenin, âhirine kadar okunup da rükû‘a gidilecek olursa namazın rükû‘ve sücûduyla secde-i tilâvet sâkıt olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oaths direct attention to temporal events that show worldly change, move from darkness to light and grief to joy, and indicate the Creator’s lordship.
rows.anchor: âlemdeki inkılâbâta delâlet eyleyen ve insanı zulmetten nûra, kederden sürûra götüren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators offer many views on the definite or indefinite wording, the scope of the articles, and the identification and interpretation of the oath objects.
rows.anchor: Bunların ta‘rîf ve tenkirlerine ve “lâm”larındaki ahid veya cins veya istiğrak ihtimalleri itibariyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fajr is the first whiteness as night darkness breaks: the false dawn is vertical and the true dawn horizontal; fasting and prayer rulings attach only to the true dawn.
rows.anchor: “Fecr” mâlum ki gece karanlığının çatladığı sabahın ilk beyazlığıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is the joyful instant when the world begins moving from darkness into light, so the generic dawn is a meaningful oath, as in 81:18.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle fecir, cihânın zulmetten nûra geçmek üzere gülümsediği en neş’eli, mes‘ud bir demidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the article as specific and understand the dawn of a blessed Friday or feast; Mujahid’s reported view most immediately points to the tenth of Dhul Hijjah, the Adha feast day.
rows.anchor: Bu surette[^3] en mütebâdiri Mücâhid’den mervî olduğu üzere kurban bayramı gününün fecri olmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although generic dawn includes the feast dawn, the particular dawn more strongly conveys the collective joy of the occasion.
rows.anchor: Evvelki buna dahi şâmil olursa da bunda daha ziyade bir hususiyet ve cem‘iyyet ile sürûra işaret vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights most readily mean the first ten nights of Dhul Hijjah, since an unqualified ten conventionally evokes the days ending with the feast; reports also identify Ramadan’s last ten and Muharram through Ashura.
rows.anchor: ale’l-ıtlâk “aşr” denilince zilhiccenin aşrı, yani birinden bayram günü olan onuncusuna kadar onu tebâdür ettiğinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form may leave the ten nights unspecified, perhaps allowing any ten or the first ten nights before the full moon of each month.
rows.anchor: nekre olarak وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍۢ denilmesi, muayyen bir aşr maksud olmayıp bunların her birine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording can also honor the nights through emphasis, or point to a representative ten-night period rather than a fixed year; any intended period ends in dawn-like joy and preferably the Adha feast.
rows.anchor: tenvînin de sade tenkir için değil tefhıym için olarak bu gecelerin şeref-i mahsûsuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last ten of Ramadan also fit because they contain the Night of Decree and end in Eid al-Fitr; the ten nights can foreshadow the world’s lifespan and the surah’s conclusion.
rows.anchor: sonra leyle-i kadri muhtevî olması ihtimâli ve îd-i fıtra müntehî bulunması itibarı ile ramazanın aşr-i ahîri de muvâfıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authentic reports from Ibn Abbas and others identify the ten with the first ten of Dhul Hijjah.
rows.anchor: Hâkim sahih diyerek ve daha bir cemaat İbn Abbas’tan rivayet etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabir reports from the Prophet that the oath’s dawn and ten nights refer to the Adha ten; al-Tabari says this is correct because the authorities of interpretation agree.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Câbir’den de “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem عَشْرُ الأَْضْحَى,وَٱلْفَجْرِ وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍۢ’dır buyurdu” diye merfû‘an rivayet etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the ten in Moses’ appointment, completing forty nights, as Dhul Hijjah’s ten.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın mîkātında وَأَتْمَمْنَٰهَا بِعَشْرٍۢ فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةًۭ [el-A‘râf 7/142] buyurulan aşr de aşr-i zilhiccedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn Abbas says no days are better for deeds or more beloved to God than these ten, except one who gives life and wealth in jihad and returns with nothing.
rows.anchor: Ahmed ve Buhârî [5793] İbn Abbas’tan merfû‘an rivayet eylemişlerdir: “‘Günlerden hiçbiri yoktur ki onlarda amel eyyâm-ı aşirden efdal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak also report Ramadan’s last ten; Aisha says the Prophet tightened his belt, prayed through the night, and woke his family when those nights began.
rows.anchor: İbn Münzir ile İbn Ebî Hâtim İbn Abbas’tan ramazanın son aşri olduğunu da rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives Jabir’s Adha report priority because Aisha’s report concerns seeking the Night of Decree and narrates the Prophet’s practice rather than defining the oath’s ten nights.
rows.anchor: bu hadis burada mervî olan “aşr”i beyan siyâkında değil, bilhassa kadir gecesi faziletini taharrî siyâkında olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternatives remain possible, with Dhul Hijjah strongest; the oath values finite, difficult worship and striving ending in success and joy, warning against eternal loss through heedlessness and rebellion.
rows.anchor: “Leyâl-i aşr” aşr-i adhâda akvâ olmakla beraber ikisine de, hatta aşr-i muharreme de sâdık olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaf and watr can denote pairing and singling, pairing and revenge, or even and odd as nouns; as verbal nouns they can mean joining or taking vengeance.
rows.anchor: “Şef‘” ve “vetr” kelimeleri masdar ve isim olarak kullanılır, masdar olduğu zaman “eş-şef‘”

rows.speaker: Yûnus
rows.claim: Yunus reports dialectal variation: upper-Arab groups use watr with fatḥa for odd and kasra for vengeance, while Tamim uses kasra in both.
rows.anchor: Yûnus[^21] demiştir ki: “Ehl-i âliye adedde feth ile ‘vetr’, ‘zahil’de, yani öc ve intikam almak mânasında kesr[^22] ile ‘vitr’ derler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, Kisai, and Khalaf read watr with kasra; most other canonical readers use fatḥa. The majority reading is Qurayshi and refers to oddness.
rows.anchor: Burada da “el-vetr” Hamza, Kisâî, Halef-i Âşir kıraatlerinde vâv’ın kesriyle

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says kasra is Tamim’s dialect and the majority fatḥa is Quraysh’s; kasra for revenge is attested, while Asmaʿi reports two forms.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “وتر kesr ile de okunmuştur, bu Temim lügatıdır. Cumhur kıraati feth üzeredir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes generally interpret the readings numerically and exclude revenge, since the majority’s fatḥa supports only oddness and pairing with revenge is unfamiliar; revenge may remain a subtle allusion.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn burada kesr kıraatlerini[^26] de bu mânaya hamlederek intikam mânasını hiç kāle almamışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the article is generic, every created thing is even or odd, so the oath covers all things and warns that everything besides God’s face perishes.
rows.anchor: Zira eşyâ ya çift veya[^28] tek olmaktan hâlî olmaz. Bu takdirde cemî‘-i eşyâya kasem edilmiş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the article refers to a specific known set, commentators list over thirty possible referents; the author will select several of the strongest transmitted views.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı müfessirîn burada otuzdan fazla vücûh zikretmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: مُجَاهِد
rows.claim: Mujahid’s report in Bukhari identifies the even as every created thing and the odd as God, linking the oath to paired creation and God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de dahi Mücâhid’den mervî olduğu üzere وَٱلشَّفْعِ mahluk olan her şey, وَٱلْوَتْرِ Allah teâlâ.[^29]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation appears in pairs of likeness or opposites—belief and unbelief, happiness and misery, guidance and error, night and day, heaven and earth, sea and land, jinn and humans, spirit and body—while God has no partner.
rows.anchor: Her mahlûkun bir misli veya zıddı vardır ki bir şef‘teşkil ederler: Küfr ü iman, saadet ve şekāvet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine-name report says God is single and loves what is odd.
rows.anchor: Esmâ-i hüsnâ hadîsinde de إِنَّ اللهَ وِتـْرٌ يُحِبُّ الْوِتـْرَ vârid olduğu[^30] mâlumdur.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Asked about the even and odd, the Prophet says some prayers are even and some are odd; Tirmidhi calls Qatada’s route unusual, while Ibn Abi Hatim grades it sound.
rows.anchor: İmran b. Husayn radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir[^32] ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’e وَٱلشَّفْعِ وَٱلْوَتْرِ’den sual olundu

rows.speaker: إبن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Zurara b. Awfa, Ikrima, Qatada, and al-Dahhak identify the even as the day of sacrifice and the odd as the day of Arafah, fitting the Adha ten.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: Zürâre b.[^36] Evfâ ve İkrime ve ondan Katâde ve Dahhâk demişlerdir ki: Şef‘yevm-i nahr, vetr yevm-i arefedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ninth of Dhul Hijjah is odd and Arafah, while the tenth is even and the sacrifice feast; the days form a coherent sequence around the principal rites of Hajj.
rows.anchor: Kurban bayramının ilk günü zilhiccenin onuncu günü olmakla çift, dokuzuncu arefe günü tektir.

rows.speaker: Tîbî
rows.claim: Tibi says the prayer interpretation from Imran’s Prophetic report cannot be set aside and must be preferred.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf hâşiyesinde Tîbî[^40] demiştir ki: “İmran b. Husayn hadîsiyle rivayet olunan salât tefsiri Resûlullah’a merfû‘olduğu için

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan counters that Jabir’s report has a sounder chain than the report from Imran b. Husayn.
rows.anchor: Bahr’da Ebû Hayyân da der ki: “Câbir hadîsi isnadca İmran b. Husayn hadîsinden esahtır.

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the most correct meaning is that God swore by every even and every odd number without restricting the kind or number.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr demiştir ki: “En doğrusu Allah teâlâ şef‘ve vetre kasem etmiş ne şef‘den ne vetrden bir nev‘i

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says the oath is by every number, even and odd.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî Hazretleri de şef‘ve vetr her adede kasem olduğunu söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports identifying Dhul Hijjah’s nights, Arafah, and the sacrifice day best fit the sequence and surah’s purpose, include the possible senses, and urge worship during life’s limited span to attain afterlife joy.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Câbir ve İbn [5797] Abbas rivayetleri üzere aşr-i zilhicce geceleri ve arefe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by night as it passes, as in the similar wording of 74:33.
rows.anchor: Ve giderken, yani geçtiği sırada geceye kasem olsun nitekim Müddessir’de وَالَّيْلِ اِذْ اَدْبَرَ [74/33] buyurulmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original form is yesrī; the final yāʾ is omitted for rhyme, so the kasra on rāʾ does not mark jussive mood; some canonical readings retain the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: “Yesr” aslı “yesrî”dir. Fâsıla için yâ hazfolunarak râ’nın kesresiyle iktifâ olunmuştur, meczum değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, and Abu Jafar retain yāʾ in connected recitation; Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain it both in pause and connection.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, Ebû Amr, Ebû Ca‘fer kıraatlerinde vasılda, İbn Kesîr ve Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde vakıfta ve vasılda yâ ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording intensifies the idea of night traveling within the night; beyond the usual bare sense of passing, it can suggest darkness about to end and grief about to pass at the blessed pre-dawn hour.
rows.anchor: Gecenin gece gitmesi, gece içinde gece mülâhaza ettirir gibi katmerli bir ifadedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generic night and dawn have the widest scope, though the night before the feast dawn is more cohesive and splendid; some identify it as the night of gathering at Muzdalifa.
rows.anchor: bu demler sabaha yakın olan mübarek seher vakitleridir. Bu itibar ile “fecr” ve “leyl” cins için olmak daha şümullü olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether these oaths or their objects offer something worth swearing by for a person whose reason restrains wrongdoing; surely they do, as signs of guidance and blessing.
rows.anchor: Bunda: bu kasemlerde veya bu zikrolunan şeylerde aklı kendisini fenalıktan men‘edecek bir akıl sâhibi için büyük bir kasem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A complete intellect traces the changing events to their Lord; hearts amid these changes find tranquility only through remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: Bütün bu hâdisât ve inkılâbât içinde mütekallib olan kalbler Allah’ı anmadan itmi’nânı[^6] bulamaz.

rows.speaker: مُجَاهِد
rows.claim: One route to the oath’s meaning is Mujahid’s reported identification of the odd as God, making God the greatest object sworn by among these signs.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den rivayet olunduğu üzere “el-vitr”den doğrudan doğru Allah’ı anlamaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, each oath object is a divine sign, and the real oath is by the one Lord they indicate, effectively ‘by the Lord of dawn’; the question both denies and affirms to elicit this answer.
rows.anchor: bunların her birini âyât-ı[^7] ilâhiyeden biri telakkī ederek onlara kasemden asıl murad delâlet ettikleri Rabb-i Vâhid’e kasem olduğunu

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Razi reads the interrogative as emphasis: an intelligent person sees the signs in these oath objects, which point to divine unity and lordship and merit an oath through their Creator.
rows.anchor: Fahr-ı Râzî bu vechi şöyle ifade etmiştir: “هَلْ فِى ذَٰلِكَ قَسَمٌۭ bir istifhamdır. Bundan murad da tekiddir.

rows.speaker: Kādî
rows.claim: Qadi says the question implies an oath by the Lord of these matters, since emphatic oath belongs to God and people are forbidden to swear by created things.
rows.anchor: Kādî[^10] demiştir ki: ‘Bu âyet, söylediğimiz vechile, kasem bu umûrun rabbine vâki‘olduğuna delâlet eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijr derives from restraint: reason is called hijr because it prevents its possessor from evil and impropriety; dhi hijr means one of complete intellect.
rows.anchor: “Hicr” men‘ve hacr mânasından me’huz olarak akıl mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two views explain the oath’s response: it is ‘your Lord is ever watchful’ with intervening verses parenthetical, or it is omitted and the following account of punishment stands in its place.
rows.anchor: Cevap إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ’dır. Arada âyetler mu‘terizadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing means knowing as if by sight through transmitted reports and traces: the vanished peoples’ stories circulated widely, their ruins were visible, and the Quran repeatedly confirms them; the formal address to the Prophet also concerns all who know.
rows.anchor: Bu görmekten murad, kalben rü’yet, yani ilimdir[^14]. Âsâr ve ahbârdan görmüş gibi bilmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These accounts warn disbelievers, guide believers, and make the earth’s ruins examples from which to learn about worldly change, the beginning and end, and useful versus futile deeds.
rows.anchor: Bunları anlatmanın fâidesi de kâfirleri inzar, mü’minleri irşad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Khaldun’s four categories are extinct ancient Arabs (including Ad, Thamud, Tasm, and Jadis), pure Qahtanite Arabs, Arabized descendants of Ishmael including the Prophet’s line, and Arabs whose language became non-Arabized through later mixing.
rows.anchor: İbn Haldun’un da zikrettiği üzere tarihçiler Arabı Arab-ı bâide, Arab-ı âribe, Arab-ı müsta‘ribe, Arab-ı müsta‘cime diye dörde tasnif

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Genealogists trace Ad to Iram, descendant of Sam son of Noah, and explain how the ancestors’ names became tribal names, with early and later Ad groups.
rows.anchor: Nessâbûn demişlerdir ki Âd, Nûh[^18] aleyhisselâm’ın oğullarından Sâm’ın oğlu İrem’in oğlu Avs’ın oğlu Âd’ın evlâdından bir kavimdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since 53:50 says God destroyed the first Ad, many commentators identify Iram of the pillars here with the first Ad.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Necm’de وَأَنَّهُۥٓ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا ٱلْأُولَىٰ [53/50] buyurulduğuna nazaran burada da Âd-ı İrem’in Âd-ı Ûlâ olduğuna kāil olan müfessirîn daha çok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram is declined genitive with fatḥa because it is a feminine proper name that is diptote.
rows.anchor: “İrem”, ta‘rîf ve te’nîs ile gayr-i munsarif olduğundan fetha[^20] ile mecrurdur.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies Iram as the name of a tribe; another report from him says the word means ancient.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ve Katâde demişlerdir ki aynıyla bir kabile ismidir.

rows.speaker: İbn İshak
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Iram was the ancestor of all Ad, so Iram’s descendants encompass the whole Ad people.
rows.anchor: İbn İshak da demiştir ki: İrem, Âd’ın hepsinin atasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading of ‘pillars’ takes imad as a pillar or as a metaphor for the tall stature of Ad, reported from Ibn Abbas and linked to 7:69.
rows.anchor: Bu İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir.

rows.speaker: İkrime ve Mukātil
rows.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil interpret the pillars as tent poles, indicating a tent-dwelling people in the Ahqaf region.
rows.anchor: İkrime ve Mukātil demişlerdir ki göçüp kondukları evlerinin direkleri demek olup çadır halkı

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the pillars are those of buildings, since Ad erected signs on elevated ground or at passage entrances.
rows.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den mervî olduğuna göre binâlarının direkleri demektir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Rükayş
rows.claim: Abu Rukaysh says the structures of Ad are their tombs, citing a poetic line comparing them to humps of Bactrian camels.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin nakline göre Ebû Rükayş “Ürûm Âd’ın kabirleridir” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexical authorities say urum and aram can mean markers or landmarks, especially ancient monuments attributed to Ad; on this reading ‘Iram of pillars’ refers to their graves, ruins, or monuments, with ‘people of’ understood.
rows.anchor: “irem”in cem‘i olan “ârâm” gibi “ürûm” da nişan ve alâmet olarak dikilen mîl ve menar gibi şeylere ıtlak edilir.
